key_agent_trends: EU advances AI Act implementation with common rules for regulatory sandboxes and a Capgemini-led consortium supporting AI Office cyber risk assessment of GPAI models.
European Commission proposes Digital Fairness Act rules giving consumers control over AI agents that conclude contracts on their behalf.
Sovereign AI infrastructure expands with Denmark investing DKK 500 million in Gefion/DCAI alongside ongoing EU Gigafactories efforts.

stories.headline: European Commission publishes Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2487 setting common rules for AI regulatory sandboxes
stories.what_happened: On 10 November 2026 the European Commission adopted Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/2487, published in the Official Journal on 11 November 2026. It lays down detailed rules for the establishment, development, implementation, operation and supervision of AI regulatory sandboxes under the AI Act. Member States must ensure at least one national sandbox is operational by 2 August 2027. Participation is free of charge for SMEs including start-ups (with limited exceptions), and applicants must receive a decision within three months.
stories.why_it_matters: It provides legal certainty and harmonised procedures for testing innovative AI systems under supervision before market placement, supporting SME access and avoiding regulatory fragmentation across the EU.

stories.headline: Capgemini selected to lead European Commission consortium for AI safety and cyber risk assessment of advanced AI models
stories.what_happened: On 5 November 2026, Capgemini announced it had been selected by the European Commission’s AI Office to lead a consortium supporting cyber threat modeling and risk assessment of advanced AI systems under the AI Act. The consortium includes Wavestone and France’s Laboratoire National de Métrologie et d’Essais (LNE). The work focuses on assessing and mitigating cyber offence risks associated with general-purpose AI models, including developing evaluation tools and conducting technical assessments.
stories.why_it_matters: It strengthens the AI Office’s capacity to identify systemic cyber risks from GPAI models and enforce AI Act obligations as enforcement powers are active.

stories.headline: European Commission proposes Digital Fairness Act with rules for AI agents concluding consumer contracts
stories.what_happened: On 11 November 2026 the European Commission presented its proposal for a Digital Fairness Act. It includes provisions for automated systems, including AI agents, that can conclude contracts on consumers’ behalf. Traders must provide tools for consumers to set the level of autonomy, requiring express choice on first use whether confirmation is needed for every contract or based on defined criteria. Conflicts of interest must be disclosed and confirmed.
stories.why_it_matters: It adapts EU consumer protection to agentic AI commerce, shifting control to how much authority consumers delegate to AI systems.

stories.headline: Denmark invests DKK 500 million in DCAI to expand sovereign AI capacity via Gefion
stories.what_happened: On 10 November 2026, the Danish Centre for AI Innovation (DCAI), operator of the Gefion AI supercomputer, announced a DKK 500 million investment. Netcompany is investing DKK 325 million as a new shareholder, EIFO is adding DKK 150 million, and the Novo Nordisk Foundation is increasing its stake to retain a majority. The goal is to broaden access to sovereign AI infrastructure for businesses, public institutions and researchers.
stories.why_it_matters: It strengthens national sovereign AI compute capacity in Europe, supporting adoption beyond experimentation in regulated sectors.
